title: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

relationships.phenotype: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.

checks.claim: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper links homozygous truncating ABCA2 variants to global developmental delay and intellectual disability. It does not use the IDPOGSA name and does not mention poor growth, seizures or ataxia.

paragraphs.text: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder. Reported patients had global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Maddirevula et al., 2019). In one family, the affected sibs had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria and elevated low density lipoprotein levels (Aslam and Naz, 2019).

checks.claim: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Autozygome, a rich source of homozygous variants, has been successfully utilized for the high throughput identification of novel autosomal recessive disease genes.
checks.explanation: The paper frames these as homozygous, recessive variants in a neurodevelopmental phenotype. It does not explicitly call this disorder autosomal recessive or use the IDPOGSA name.

checks.claim: Reported patients with IDPOGSA had global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states the two ABCA2 families had global developmental delay and intellectual disability.

checks.claim: In one IDPOGSA family, the affected sibs had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: In one IDPOGSA family, the affected sibs had elevated low density lipoprotein levels.
checks.evidence_quote: The levels of low density lipid proteins were elevated in blood samples of both affected individuals.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) reported 2 families in which affected individuals had global developmental delay and intellectual disability. The index patient (16DG0071) of 1 family had no apparent gross dysmorphism.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) reported 2 families in which affected individuals had global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper reports two ABCA2 families with these features.

checks.claim: The index patient (16DG0071) of 1 family reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019) had no apparent gross dysmorphism.
checks.evidence_quote: Facial pictures of index (16DG0071) subject with ABCA2 showing apparent lack of gross dysmorphism.
checks.explanation: The Figure 2 legend states this directly for patient 16DG0071.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family who had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. Brain MRI of the older sib showed no abnormalities. Both affected sibs had elevated blood levels of low density lipoproteins.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family.
checks.evidence_quote: We performed clinical assessments and magnetic resonance imaging of the older of two siblings affected with a movement disorder.
checks.explanation: The family is described as consanguineous and Pakistani, with two affected siblings.

checks.claim: The 2 sibs from the consanguineous Pakistani family studied by Aslam and Naz (2019) had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Brain MRI of the older affected sib in the Pakistani family studied by Aslam and Naz (2019) showed no abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Magnetic resonance imaging did not reveal brain abnormalities.
checks.explanation: The methods say MRI was done on the older sibling, and the results say it showed no abnormalities.

checks.claim: Both affected sibs in the Pakistani family studied by Aslam and Naz (2019) had elevated blood levels of low density lipoproteins.
checks.evidence_quote: The levels of low density lipid proteins were elevated in blood samples of both affected individuals.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of IDPOGSA in the families reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019) and in the consanguineous Pakistani family reported by Aslam and Naz (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of IDPOGSA in the families reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Homozygous variants in the autozygome that fully segregate with the disorder are consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of IDPOGSA in the consanguineous Pakistani family reported by Aslam and Naz (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: The study was conducted to identify the molecular basis of a movement disorder in a consanguineous Pakistani family.
checks.explanation: Consanguinity and segregation of the variant suggest recessive inheritance, but the abstract does not state that the pattern was autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability, Maddirevula et al. (2019) used autozygome and exome analysis to identify homozygous truncating mutations in the ABCA2 gene (c.740dupT, p.Gly248Argfs*38 and c.1027C-T, p.Gln343Ter; NM_212533.2). The variants fully segregated with the disorder in the families. The authors suggested that the phenotype was distinct from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reported by Steinberg et al., and might represent a distinct allelic disorder.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) studied affected members of 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper describes two families with these features.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) used autozygome and exome analysis to identify homozygous truncating ABCA2 mutations in 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: METHODS: Autozygome and exome analysis of patients with suspected Mendelian phenotypes.
checks.explanation: The methods and results together support autozygome/exome identification of homozygous truncating ABCA2 variants in 2 families.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified the homozygous truncating ABCA2 mutation c.740dupT (p.Gly248Argfs*38; NM_212533.2).
checks.evidence_quote: homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38])
checks.explanation: The variant and transcript match the paper exactly.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified the homozygous truncating ABCA2 mutation c.1027C-T (p.Gln343Ter; NM_212533.2).
checks.explanation: The variant and transcript match the paper; p.Gln343* is the same as p.Gln343Ter.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 variants identified by Maddirevula et al. (2019) fully segregated with the disorder in the families.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states the variants fully segregated.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) suggested that the ABCA2-related phenotype in their families was distinct from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reported by Steinberg et al.
checks.evidence_quote: which is distinct from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reported by Steinberg et al.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the paper.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) suggested that the ABCA2-related phenotype in their families might represent a distinct allelic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: In class 3, the phenotypes observed are sufficiently different from those previously reported that we argue these may represent distinct allelic disorders (Supplementary Table 1, Fig. 2). These include two families
checks.explanation: The paper places the ABCA2 families in class 3, its category for possible distinct allelic disorders.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria, Aslam and Naz (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous 1-bp deletion in the ABCA2 gene (c.4993delG, NM_212533.2), predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Val1665TyrfsTer36). Sanger sequencing confirmed segregation of the mutation with the disorder. The variant was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls. The authors noted that the phenotype was highly concordant with that seen in Abca2 knockout mice.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) used whole-exome sequencing in 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analyses included whole-exome sequencing in order to delineate the underlying pathology of the disorder.
checks.explanation: Whole-exome sequencing is stated in the methods.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) identified a homozygous 1-bp deletion in the ABCA2 gene (c.4993delG, NM_212533.2) in 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing data analyses identified a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36) in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2) which segregated with the disorder
checks.explanation: The variant and transcript match, but the abstract does not say the variant was homozygous. That detail may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.4993delG deletion is predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Val1665TyrfsTer36).
checks.evidence_quote: identified a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36) in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2)
checks.explanation: The abstract calls it a frameshift, and Ter36 indicates premature termination.

checks.claim: Sanger sequencing confirmed segregation of the ABCA2 c.4993delG mutation with the disorder in the Pakistani family.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation of variants with the phenotype was checked by Sanger sequencing.
checks.explanation: The results also state that the variant segregated with the disorder.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.4993delG variant was absent from all publicly available databases.
checks.evidence_quote: was absent from all publicly available databases and ethnically matched controls
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.4993delG variant was absent from ethnically matched controls.
checks.evidence_quote: was absent from all publicly available databases and ethnically matched controls
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) noted that the phenotype of the Pakistani sibs with ABCA2 c.4993delG was highly concordant with that seen in Abca2 knockout mice.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotype observed in our patients shows high concordance with that observed in Abca2 knockout mice.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (IDPOGSA), Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified a homozygous 1-bp duplication (c.740dupT, NM_212533.2) in the ABCA2 gene, predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Gly248ArgfsTer38). The mutation, identified by autozygome and exome analysis, fully segregated with the disorder in the family.

checks.evidence_quote: homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38])
checks.explanation: The paper reports this homozygous duplication in a family with global developmental delay and intellectual disability. The IDPOGSA label comes from the draft, not the paper.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.740dupT duplication is predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Gly248ArgfsTer38).
checks.evidence_quote: homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38])

checks.explanation: The paper states the variants fully segregated.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (IDPOGSA), Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified a homozygous c.1027C-T transition (c.1027C-T, NM_212533.2) in the ABCA2 gene, resulting in a gln343-to-ter (Q343X) substitution. The mutation, identified by autozygome and exome analysis, fully segregated with the disorder in the family.

checks.explanation: The paper reports c.1027C>T as homozygous in one of the two families. The IDPOGSA label comes from the draft, not the paper.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.1027C-T transition results in a gln343-to-ter (Q343X) substitution.
checks.explanation: p.Gln343* is the same as Q343X.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.1027C-T mutation was identified by autozygome and exome analysis.

checks.explanation: The study identified its variants by autozygome and exome analysis.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.1027C-T mutation fully segregated with the disorder in the family reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019).
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states the variants fully segregated.
